nodes.question: How do households influence high waste generation in industries?
nodes.answer: Households influence high waste generation in industries by consuming industry goods, thereby driving demand which is impacted by consumer culture and built-in obsolescence from capitalist industries.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Product life-cycle analysis|Waste generation_qna_002
nodes.label: Ethics and regulation
nodes.question: How is the concept of waste generation linked to advertising in the household consumer context?
nodes.answer: If households do not succumb to advertising's messaging about superiority, it could lead to reduced waste generation and no market for industry goods.
nodes.paragraph: In turn, advertising appeals to the desire for status by promoting consumption, early disposal, and ownership of the latest trends. The desire to appear superior to others, is the basis of social hierarchies. What gets disposed as waste is shaped by monopolistic corporate power: at one end manufactur - ers, marketers and ad men, at the other giant corporations and the notion that garbage is good for business (Rogers 2005, p. 9). Our study focuses attention on the household consumers, who are also household solid waste generators. If households do not yield to advertising messaging about superiority, there will be reduced waste generation and no market for industry goods. Reduced demand for goods defies the capitalist notion of acquisition of wealth as a means to gain power (Bookchin 2007, p. 7 of 12). Tackling this social hierarchy, would be the first step to addressing socio- ecological problems as explained by Bookchin (1993). This study adds to the growing inventory of easily acces- sible, user relevant solutions to waste management. Cop- ies of this research will be available in national and district libraries, providing insights for policymakers and commu- nity leaders to inform new policy directions.

nodes.question: How can the efficiency of a process be understood using the waste generation rate equation?
nodes.answer: The efficiency of a process can be understood by calculating the Waste Generation Rate, which is determined by dividing the Total Waste Generated by the Total Production Output, as per Equation (3).

nodes.question: How much waste generation is involved in the spinning phase when 2.5 kg of cotton fibre is used?
nodes.answer: In the spinning phase when 2.5 kg of cotton fibre is used, the waste generation ranges from 0.126 to 0.254 kg.
